title: Voice: barge-in over a playing reply on a phone whose echo canceller fails (−14 dB of its own reply in the mic)

personas.persona: A busy owner who changes their mind quickly and talks over the AI when an answer goes the wrong way.
goals: Ask main to tell you, in about thirty seconds, the story of how the Python language got its name and its early history.

A few seconds into that answer, interrupt it (barge in) with a different question: what is three hundred and forty two times seven. Plan it in during_reply: [{"at_s":5,"text":"actually forget that, just tell me what three hundred forty two times seven is, over"}]
Hear the answer to the new question (2394), then finish.
script: First turn: the history request with the during_reply barge-in above.
If you heard the number, finish; otherwise ask once more.

voice_checks.name: the barge-in was heard by the box and answered out loud (AEC failing: advisory)
the interrupted reply stopped early (AEC failing: advisory)
the echo of the reply never reached MAIN as words

note: echo 0.2 models an AEC that is not working (speakerphone at full volume, a cheap device): the reply's audio keeps the mic's speech detector open, so one segment spans the whole reply and its final only lands when the reply ends. The product must keep the echo out of MAIN; a barge-in can only be heard once the reply is over (advisory), and the reply cannot be cut (advisory).
